newsitem.title: GERMANY: Merrill - Recent EMU events worry U.S. investors.
newsitem.headline: Merrill - Recent EMU events worry U.S. investors.

text.p: U.S. institutional investors grew more worried about the impact of European monetary union on German equities over the last couple of months, but still remain committed to the market, a top executive at U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch and Co Inc said on Wednesday.

Speaking at a media briefing, Thomas Davis, New York-based co-head of Merrill's Corporate and Institutional Client group, said that he did not expect foreign investors to be overly worried about German investments ahead of the launch of a single currency in 1999.
But he added that worries about monetary union over the last two months had led to a "heightened sense of concern" among U.S. institutional investors.

Over the last two months, the future of monetary union was cast into doubt by a public fight between the Bundesbank and Bonn over revaluing German official reserves and disagreements over a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline after the start of monetary union in 1999.
Davis added U.S. institutional investors appeared to be more worried about the durability of monetary union than are investors in Europe.

Andreas Von Buddenbrock, Merrill's managing director, investment banking in Frankfurt, said the bank will expand the number of professionals in investment banking and equity trading and research by around 35 percent in the next 18 months from 100 now in its Frankfurt office.
He said Merrill Lynch expected demand for such activities to climb as Germany develops a shareholder culture and smaller companies consider raising funds on the equity markets.
Merrill Lynch employs a total of 200 people in Frankfurt.
